title: Settings-test temp-path race STILL present: nanosecond-unique paths collide under Odin's parallel test runner on macOS — a pristine full `odin test app` run failed 2/10 times at the reviewed sha
evidence: tmp_settings_path: `path := strings.concatenate({dir, "/pp-settings-test-", fmt.tprintf("%d", time.to_unix_nanoseconds(now))}, context.temp_allocator); os.remove(path)`. Clock-resolution probe on this machine: `repeats: 196581` of 200000 back-to-back `time.to_unix_nanoseconds(time.now())` calls return the SAME value. Pristine-copy 10x `odin test app`: run 6 -> `2 tests failed. - main.settings_round_trip 'round-trip must restore the saved settings' - main.settings_startup_apply 'startup applies the scale step'`; other 9 runs green.
detail: Briefing spot-check demands 'repeated full odin test app runs must stay green'. They do not: ~µs clock resolution means parallel tests land on one path, and tmp_settings_path's os.remove deletes another test's fixture. Intermittent gate-2 red (~10%/run, worse across the 3x repeat leg).
recommended_fix: Make paths collision-free under parallelism: add an atomic per-process counter and/or os.getpid, or a random suffix from a per-test Rng (e.g. path + pid + atomic increment). Never os.remove a path another test may own.
